<task type="checkpoint:human-verify" gate="blocking-human">
  <name>Task 1: Package-legitimacy gate for p-queue (blocking, not auto-approvable)</name>
  <what-built>
Nothing yet — this gate runs BEFORE the install. RESEARCH.md's Package Legitimacy Audit tagged `p-queue`
as `[ASSUMED]`, not `[VERIFIED]`: the automated `package-legitimacy check` seam was not invokable in the
research environment, so the verdict rests on manual signals only (`npm view p-queue version` ->
`9.3.3`, `npm view p-queue engines` -> `{ node: '>=20' }`, and a README consistent with the
long-established `sindresorhus/p-queue` project). No `[SLOP]` or `[SUS]` packages were found.

`p-queue` is the single package this phase adds. It is the concurrency-cap and pause/resume primitive
behind SAFE-01 and SAFE-02.
  </what-built>
  <how-to-verify>
1. Open https://www.npmjs.com/package/p-queue in a browser.
2. Confirm the repository link resolves to `github.com/sindresorhus/p-queue` (not a lookalike org).
3. Confirm the latest published version is `9.3.3` or a later `9.x`, and that the publish date is not
   within the last 72 hours (a brand-new publish on a mature package warrants a second look).
4. Confirm the weekly download count is in the millions, consistent with a widely-depended-on package.
5. In a terminal, run: `npm view p-queue scripts.postinstall` — it must print nothing (an empty result).
   Any install-time script on this package is a stop signal.
6. Optionally run `gsd-tools query package-legitimacy check --ecosystem npm p-queue` if that tool is
   available in this environment; RESEARCH.md explicitly asks for this as the final gate.

This checkpoint is NOT auto-approvable. `workflow.auto_advance` does not apply to package-legitimacy
checkpoints.
  </how-to-verify>
  <resume-signal>Type "approved" to proceed to the install, or describe what looked wrong.</resume-signal>
</task>

<task type="auto">
  <name>Task 2: Install p-queue at ^9.3.3 and confirm the ESM import resolves</name>
  <precondition>The package-legitimacy checkpoint above returned "approved" and `npm view p-queue scripts.postinstall` printed nothing.</precondition>
  <files>package.json, package-lock.json</files>
  <read_first>
    - package.json (the `dependencies` block; note `"type": "module"` on line 5 and `engines.node >= 22`)
    - .planning/phases/02-execution-worktree-runner-billing-safety/02-RESEARCH.md (section "Standard Stack" — `p-queue` row; and "State of the Art" — the CLAUDE.md `8.x` figure is stale)
  </read_first>
  <action>
Run `npm install p-queue@^9.3.3` so the entry lands in `dependencies` (not `devDependencies` — the
daemon needs it at runtime). Pin `^9.3.3`, NOT `^8.x`: `./.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s Section B stack table
lists `8.x`, and RESEARCH.md confirmed live via `npm view p-queue version` that `9.3.3` is current and
that `9.x` declares `engines.node >= 20`, compatible with this project's `>= 22`. `p-queue` 9 is
ESM-only, which matches this project's `"type": "module"`; do not add any CJS interop shim.

Do not install any other package in this task. In particular do not add `bullmq`, `redis`, or any other
queue backend — CLAUDE.md's "What NOT to Use" table rejects them for a single-user, single-box daemon,
and `p-queue`'s documented surface (`.pause()`, `.start()`, `.clear()`, the settable `.concurrency`
property, `.pending`, `.size`, `.isPaused`) already covers every control D-25 and D-27 need. Also leave
`execa` in `devDependencies` untouched — it stays for Phase 1's existing use, and CONTEXT.md D-13
deliberately selects `node:child_process` for all new runner code.

Verify the import resolves in this project's module system by running a one-line `tsx` evaluation that
imports `PQueue` from `p-queue`, constructs `new PQueue({ concurrency: 3 })`, and prints its
`concurrency` and `isPaused` values. This catches an ESM/CJS resolution failure at install time rather
than in the middle of plan 02-04's tracer.
  </action>
  <verify>
    <automated>node -e "const p=require('./package.json');const v=p.dependencies['p-queue'];if(!v||!/^\^9\./.test(v)){console.error('p-queue not pinned at ^9.x, got: '+v);process.exit(1)}console.log('OK '+v)"</automated>
  </verify>
  <acceptance_criteria>
    - `package.json`'s `dependencies` contains a `p-queue` key whose value matches `^9.` (asserted by the verify command above, which exits non-zero otherwise).
    - `p-queue` does NOT appear in `devDependencies`.
    - `package-lock.json` is updated and committed alongside `package.json`.
    - `npx tsx --eval "import PQueue from 'p-queue'; const q = new PQueue({ concurrency: 3 }); console.log(q.concurrency, q.isPaused);"` prints `3 false` and exits 0.
    - `npm test` still exits 0 (the install broke nothing).
    - `npm view p-queue scripts.postinstall` printed nothing during the preceding checkpoint.
  </acceptance_criteria>
  <done>`p-queue@^9.x` is a runtime dependency and importable under this project's ESM configuration.</done>
</task>

<task type="checkpoint:decision" gate="blocking">
  <name>Task 3: Confirm the one-way D-03 decision before any spawn argv is written</name>
  <decision>
Confirm CONTEXT.md D-03: `--bare` is prohibited outright in every `claude` spawn Fleet builds, and a
test asserts it never appears in spawn argv. This is rated **one-way** in CONTEXT.md.
  </decision>
  <context>
`--bare` skips hook/skill/plugin/MCP/CLAUDE.md auto-discovery and, per the installed CLI's own `--help`
text, bare-mode auth "is strictly `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `apiKeyHelper` via `--settings` (OAuth and
keychain are never read)." That is precisely the per-token API-billing path this project exists to avoid.

Why this door is one-way rather than merely costly: adopting `--bare` at any later point would require
provisioning an API key for the worker, which contradicts PROJECT.md's stated hard constraint
("Subscription-only Claude Code operation — never API-key billing") and would invalidate every
BILL-01…BILL-08 guarantee this phase builds. The undo is not a refactor; it is abandoning the project's
central premise. Confirming here means every spawn-argv builder from plan 02-04 onward is written
against the no-`--bare` contract and asserted by a test, and Phase 3's hook configuration must travel
in inline `--settings` JSON rather than relying on bare mode's discovery behavior.

CONTEXT.md's `### Claude's Discretion` section notes the user delegated all four decision areas with
"use best practices for everything" — so this specific option was chosen by Claude, not stated by the
developer, which is why it is being surfaced rather than assumed.
  </context>
  <options>
    <option id="confirm-d03">
      <name>Confirm: prohibit `--bare` outright, enforced by a test</name>
      <pros>Preserves subscription-only billing structurally. Keeps the D-01 resolution (`--setting-sources ""` plus inline `--settings`) coherent — settings-source pinning and OAuth login are orthogonal, so Fleet gets scope isolation without touching auth. Matches PROJECT.md's hard constraint with zero exceptions to remember.</pros>
      <cons>Fleet inherits whatever hook/skill/plugin auto-discovery the CLI performs by default, mitigated by `--setting-sources ""`. Phase 3's per-worktree hook URLs must be delivered via inline `--settings` JSON rather than a written settings file.</cons>
    </option>
    <option id="revisit-d03">
      <name>Revisit: allow `--bare` behind an explicit opt-in flag</name>
      <pros>Would give the leanest, most deterministic worker startup, with no ambient discovery at all.</pros>
      <cons>Requires an API key or `apiKeyHelper` in the worker's reach, which is the exact failure mode BILL-01…BILL-08 exist to prevent and which PROJECT.md forbids. Would make the D-02 `apiKeySource === "none"` assertion unsatisfiable.</cons>
    </option>
  </options>
  <resume-signal>Select: confirm-d03 or revisit-d03.</resume-signal>
</task>

</tasks>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| npm registry -> this repository's `node_modules` | An install-time script or a typosquatted package executes with the developer's full privileges |
| Fleet spawn argv -> `claude` CLI auth resolution | The flags Fleet chooses determine whether the session bills against the subscription or against an API key |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-2-SC | Tampering | `npm install p-queue` | high | mitigate | Blocking human legitimacy checkpoint (Task 1) verifying the repo link, version, and download profile at `npmjs.com/package/p-queue`, plus an `npm view p-queue scripts.postinstall` gate; not auto-approvable |
| T-2-04 | Information Disclosure | `claude` spawn auth mode | critical | mitigate | Task 3 confirms D-03's outright `--bare` prohibition, keeping OAuth/keychain auth reachable so `apiKeySource` can stay `none`; plan 02-04 asserts the flag is absent from every built argv |
</threat_model>
